title: Claim Filing and Appeal Time Limits, Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program
content:
Every payer time limit on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program is a count of calendar days, and each limit runs from its own starting date.

| Tier | Original claim filing limit, days from the ship date | Corrected claim after a CO-16 denial, days from the denial's posting date | First-level appeal, days from the denial's posting date | Second-level appeal, days from the posting date of the first-level decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Testing Supplies Self-Pay Program | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial HMO Program | 90 | 90 | 180 | 120 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial PPO Program | 180 | 180 | 180 | 120 |
| Testing Supplies Medicare Advantage Program | 180 | 180 | 65 | 0 |
| Testing Supplies Original Medicare Program | 365 | 365 | 120 | 180 |
| Testing Supplies Medicaid Program | 365 | 365 | 60 | 120 |

**Meaning of a zero**

- Filing limit 0: no payer claim is filed on the tier.
- Corrected-claim window 0: not applicable.
- First-level appeal 0: no payer appeal exists.
- Second-level appeal 0: there is no customer-filed second level. On the self-pay tier there is none at all; on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan itself forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity.

**Names of the levels**

| Level | Commercial tiers | Medicare Advantage | Original Medicare | Medicaid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First level | internal appeal | reconsideration | redetermination | plan appeal |
| Second level | external review | forwarded by the plan | QIC reconsideration | state fair hearing |

The ship date is the date of service for the filing limit. A first-level appeal window counts from the posting date of the denial being appealed; a second-level window counts from the posting date of the first-level decision.
